title: NAND Flash Memory: Floating-Gate Quantum Tunneling & Physical Bit Storage in USB Drives
topic: Solid-State Quantum Electronics & Non-Volatile Memory Physics
pedagogical_goal: Demonstrate the atomic-scale physical mechanism of USB flash drives: how a Floating-Gate Transistor traps electrons via Fowler-Nordheim Quantum Tunneling through an 8nm SiO2 oxide barrier to store bits ('0' vs '1') non-volatiles without battery power, and how threshold voltage shift (Vth) is sensed during read operations.

quantum_and_electrostatic_laws: Fowler-Nordheim Quantum Tunneling Current: J_FN = A * E^2 * exp(-B / E)
Threshold Voltage Shift: Delta_Vth = Q_fg / C_pp = (q * N_electrons) / C_pp
MOSFET Channel Current: I_ds = mu * C_ox * (W/L) * (V_cg - V_th)^2 when V_cg > V_th, else 0
Gauss's Law & Electrostatic Shielding: E_channel = (V_cg - q * N_e / C_fg) / d_dielectric

components.description: Golden glowing electron particles trapped inside the floating gate rectangle, increasing in density as stored charge increases.
Purple wave arrows showing Fowler-Nordheim quantum tunneling through the 8nm oxide barrier during write (+18V) or erase (-20V).
Green conduction electrons flowing from Source to Drain through the inversion channel when Vcg > Vth during Read mode.
Small side graph showing the energy barrier tilt under high electric field, illustrating quantum wave penetration.

telemetry_metrics.label: Sensed Binary Bit
telemetry_metrics.description: State '0' corresponds to trapped electrons shielding the gate; '1' corresponds to empty floating gate.

telemetry_metrics.label: Threshold Voltage (Vth)
telemetry_metrics.description: Minimum gate voltage required to invert channel. Trapped electrons shift Vth from ~1.5V up to ~5.5V.

telemetry_metrics.label: Channel Conduction
telemetry_metrics.description: Sense amplifier at Bit Line measures whether current flows to determine 1 vs 0.

telemetry_metrics.label: Source-Drain Current (Ids)
telemetry_metrics.description: Conduction current detected by the USB drive's sense amplifier.

telemetry_metrics.label: Oxide Electric Field (E_ox)
telemetry_metrics.description: Fields exceeding ~10 MV/cm trigger Fowler-Nordheim quantum tunneling through the energy barrier.

telemetry_metrics.label: Estimated Data Retention
telemetry_metrics.description: Isolated by high-energy SiO2 barriers (3.1 eV), trapped electrons remain stable for decades without power.

educational_callouts.title: Why It Never Forgets (Non-Volatile)
educational_callouts.text: Unlike RAM which needs continuous electricity to refresh capacitor charge, the Floating Gate is completely surrounded by glass-like silicon dioxide insulators. The 3.1 eV energy barrier is so high that trapped electrons cannot escape at room temperature for over 10 to 50 years.

educational_callouts.title: Quantum Tunneling vs Classical Physics
educational_callouts.text: Classically, electrons cannot climb over the 3.1 eV SiO2 barrier with normal thermal energy. Under high voltage (18V), the oxide band tilts so sharply that the barrier thickness narrows to a few nanometers. Electrons exploit quantum mechanical wave-particle duality to tunnel directly through the barrier into the floating gate.

educational_callouts.title: How a Pendrive Reads a Bit
educational_callouts.text: The USB memory controller applies a gentle read voltage of +2.5V to the control gate. If electrons are trapped (Bit 0), their negative charge repels electrons in the silicon below, preventing a channel and yielding 0 µA current. If the gate is empty (Bit 1), the +2.5V attracts electrons, turning the transistor ON and conducting current.
